Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Ramirez, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech had a productive second quarter, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
2. New product launches and contribution to growth
3. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
4. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
5. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
6. Key assumptions underlying the guidance

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Global procedure volumes grew 15.3% year-over-year in the second quarter, accelerating from 12.8% in the first quarter. This is the strongest quarterly increase since the fourth quarter of 2021 and reflects a solid rebound in elective and semi-elective cases across our core franchises. Utilization rates in hospital operating rooms averaged 92% of 2019 levels globally, up from 87% in the prior quarter, thanks to resolved staffing backlogs and better bed turnover. We've noted particular strength in high-acuity procedures, where our premium products like the next-gen EvoGuard TAVR valve and PrecisionFlow neuromodulation leads command 20-25% premium average selling prices over legacy competitors. MedSurg volumes rose 16% and Cardiovascular up 12%, driving our organic revenue growth of 14.2%.

By therapeutic area, trends were strong and differentiated. In Cardiovascular, volumes increased 17%, powered by a 22% surge in structural heart procedures, including TAVR and TMVR cases similar to MitraClip. TAVR grew 24% year-over-year, benefiting from expanded indications for lower-risk patients based on recent EARLY TAVR III data, much like Boston Scientific's Lotus Edge momentum. PCI volumes rose 14%, with our Xcelerate drug-eluting stents gaining 2.2 points of share from Abbott's Xience family due to superior deliverability in calcified lesions. Orthopedics saw 18% growth, led by a 25% ramp in robotic-assisted THA and TKA procedures. Our Rio Robotics system, inspired by Mako, reached 85,000 cumulative cases, with same-system utilization up 28% quarter-over-quarter as hospitals improve OR throughput. Cementless implants grew 19%, driven by our porous titanium Trinity stems that cut subsidence rates by 15% in post-market surveillance. MedSurg and Neuro combined for 13% growth, with endoscopy at 16% thanks to single-use scopes like PureView duodenoscopes achieving 45% attach rates in top IDNs to address CRE infection risks. Spine procedures rose 14%, aided by minimally invasive fusions using NanoFuse biologics, though slightly moderated by elective backlog pull-forwards.

Regionally, recovery is asynchronous but positive overall. In the U.S., comprising 62% of revenue, volumes jumped 18.5% year-over-year, with OR utilization at 95% of 2019 peaks. CMS reimbursement stability under the 2023 OPPS final rule, including a 2.7% inflation update, unlocked pent-up demand. IDN consolidation at places like Kaiser and HCA drove 20% growth in bundled payment models, where our value-based care kits saved 12% per case. Europe, at 22% of revenue, grew 11%, lagging due to energy costs and NHS waitlists over 7 million cases, but Germany and France led at 14% with DRG optimizations for TAVR under G-DRG E70Z. The UK was flat sequentially amid industrial action, but we're gaining with NICE endorsements for neuromodulation in chronic migraine. Asia-Pacific, 10% of revenue, shone with 25% growth; China up 32% on NRDL inclusions for TAVR and robotics, hitting over 15,000 procedures versus 8,000 last year. Japan grew 18% post-PMDRF approvals, and India ramped endoscopy 30% with affordable single-use options. Emerging markets at 6% grew 22%, led by Brazil's SUS expansions and Middle East investments in da Vinci-like robotics, supported by our Vietnam hub mitigating Red Sea issues.

Our AI-driven Procedure Optimization Suite, live in 1,200 ORs, boosted case throughput 18% via predictive scheduling, similar to Stryker's Mako but with inventory management. The EDGE Clinical Pathways program partners with 150 KOLs for hybrid AFib ablations using Symplicity Spyral RDN catheter, driving 30% adoption in EP labs. Market recovery is 75% complete for electives per clinician surveys, with remaining backlogs in orthopedics and spine amid a 15% surgeon shortage projected by 2028 per AAMC. Our Talent Accelerator academies trained 2,500 reps and techs year-to-date. We gained 110 basis points share in Q2, reaching 18% global leadership in structural heart. For Q3, we guide 14-16% procedure growth, full-year organic 13-15%. Risks include U.S. recession deferrals or Eurozone tightening, but 65% recurring revenue insulates us.

Now, let's talk about new product launches and contribution to growth.

New product revenue from launches in the past 24 months totaled $285 million in the quarter, up 42% year-over-year and 22% of our $1.3 billion total device revenue. This is the third straight quarter above 20% mix, aligning with our Investor Day target for mid-teens organic growth. These products averaged 72% gross margins, a 450 basis point premium over legacy, thanks to higher-value tech and lower costs from Galway automation.

Leading is VitaFlow Neo transcatheter heart valve, U.S. launched late 2023 post-510(k) and breakthrough designation for its leaflet design and nitinol frame. It targets the 14% CAGR structural heart market per Grand View Research. Q3 sales hit $112 million, U.S. up 65% sequentially on CY2024 OPPS Medicare boosts adding 3.2% to ASPs. Internationally, CE Mark renewal and German/Italian tenders added $28 million, 25% of total. Europe penetration at 12% vs. Abbott MitraClip and Edwards Sapien, with TRIDENT-2 trial data showing 95% success and 2.1% 30-day mortality fueling adoption.

OrthoAI suite, with AI-optimized 3D-printed tibial implants and navigation, rolled out in EU5 and APAC, tapping $18 billion orthopedics where digital tools grow 22% CAGR per IDC. Sales $92 million, up 55%, 75% margins from AI cutting revisions 18% in 5,000 cases. APAC starred, China doubling to $35 million via Mindray partnership and NRDL for knee devices. U.S. ramping post-FDA, targeting 15% robotics ortho share by 2025 vs. Stryker Mako and Zimmer ROSA.

CoreBot v2.0 minimally invasive robotics with haptic feedback and 7DOF arms added $81 million, up 35%, in $12 billion market growing 17% per MedTech Dive. 180 systems placed, 22 cases/month utilization. EMEA 40% of sales via UK NHS, India $12 million on cost advantages over da Vinci.

Our 'Innovate to Penetrate' invests 12.5% revenue in R&D, digital twins, Synergy Ventures M&A like $450 million AI imaging buy. Filed three IDEs including bioresorbable peripheral stent, aiming 25% new mix by FY2025. Risks: supply volatility for robotics magnets, CMS IRA cuts, but 18-month inventory buffers. These drove 65% organic growth, expanding TAM to $150 billion.

Moving on to capital equipment vs consumables mix trends.

Capital equipment was 32% of our $2.8 billion Q3 revenue, or $896 million up 4% organically, while consumables at 68% or $1.9 billion surged 16%. Fifth straight quarter consumables outpacing capital double-digits, trailing 12-month mix at record 67% vs. 62% ago, ahead of 55-60% peer average like Stryker, Boston Scientific.

In Structural Heart, Apex TAVR delivery consoles grew 3%, but consumables 22% on 14% installed base to 4,200 systems, $28,000 ASPs firm, 92% U.S. utilization via AI optimization boosting OR efficiency 18%. Electrophysiology: $210 million capital flat, 5% ASP to $145,000 on contact-force; consumables $620 million up 19%, FlexiMap 15% AFib share per Millennium.

U.S. 52% revenue, consumables mix 71% up 500 bps on CMS VBP neuromod leads, 20% ASC ramp like Abbott Navitor. EMEA 28%, consumables 14% amid German DRG, offset 2% capital dip via Siemens imaging. APAC 18% growth, China consumables 25% post-NMPA Renal Denervation to 72% mix. LATAM tailwinds, Brazil endoscopy clips 30%.

Pillars accelerating: Innovation like Horizon modular robotics ortho, 40% lower service, Gen3 implants 25% durability for 150 bps mix expansion 2025; R&D up 8% to $420 million on single-use antimicrobial guidewires. Commercial: 1.15x utilization to 1.25x via MediConnect analytics for 10-15% uplifts like Edwards Octave; NeuroVance M&A adds $150 million DBS leads, 300 bps. Capital discipline: 3.2x LTV vs. 2.5x peers.

FY24 consumables 68-69%, 14-16% growth vs. capital 5-7%. Risks: U.S. reimbursement, China delays; tailwinds GLP-1 offsets, demographics. De-risks 75%+ margins, 12-15% EPS CAGR.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

We achieved 68.2% non-GAAP gross margin, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 90 sequentially, sixth straight expansion quarter at high end of peers like Intuitive da Vinci or Stryker ortho. GAAP 66.5% after $12 million SBC/amortization.

Drivers: 140 bps from mix, premium structural heart like TAVR valves now 28% cardiology revenues up from 22%, 80%+ margins on single-use shift to value-based. Commodity stents/pacing down deliberately. Pricing 80 bps, ASPs +2.1% global, 3-4% U.S. robotics like PrecisionNav vs. Medtronic StealthStation; EMEA bundling vs. UK HTA; China NMPA stents. Costs 120 bps favorability, Costa Rica facility 95% utilization, Six Sigma +18% output; $25 million robotic packaging savings for NeuroStim DBS, scrap 2.1% to 1.4%. Raw materials inflation 50 bps offset by hedging.

U.S. +250 bps to 71% on ASC Medicare; Europe flat 65% German DRG offset; APAC +300 to 64% Japan neuro. Q4 guide 68.5-69.5%, FY24 +100-150 bps to 70%+ by mid-2025 via AI imaging, biologics integration.

Supply chain: 98.2% on-time delivery vs. 94% industry. Inventory 7.2 months, down 5% seq. Diversified single-source 22% to 14%, dual 85% CMOS endoscopy like Boston Scientific. Nearshoring: Querétaro Mexico EP catheters, 40% lead times, $150 million CapEx to 30% NA by FY25. APAC watch: Shanghai 40% neurovascular, pivot Vietnam/India rare earths vs. U.S. controls; freight $4,200/container down 25%. Taiwan stress-tested, 90 days ASIC buffer; 70% 2024 resins locked mid-single digits Dow/Sabic.

Now, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

SG&A was $352 million, up 3% year-over-year but flat sequentially, vs. 8% revenue growth to $1.21 billion, down 180 bps to 29.1%—lowest in three years. Adjusted 27.8% excluding FX EMEA and restructuring from peripheral vascular integration like Boston BTG. Fourth straight sequential improvement, better than Stryker/Abbott mid-30s.

Selling 62% at $218 million up 2% despite 12% U.S. cardio sales force ramp for TAVR. Sales Force Optimization 2.0 with AI territory mapping Salesforce Einstein/Veeva cut travel 22%, productivity $2.8 million/rep up 15% vs. Medtronic $2.4 million. Digital/VR 35% interactions, demo costs -18%.

G&A 38% down 1% to $134 million. ZBB year two saved $28 million or 8%, Bangalore SSC consolidated -12% headcount for ortho/endoscopy. SAP Ariba/blockchain procurement -9% indirect like J&J DePuy.

U.S. 58% revenue, efficiency +250 bps to 28.5% via value-based IDN commissions cap 5% vs. 11% procedures. EMEA 22%, +320 bps to 31.2% Munich/London hubs telemedicine EP. APAC 15% growth flat 25% China right-sizing post-NMPA. LATAM 5% Brazil tenders.

Targeting 100-150 bps FY leverage: GenAI contracts/tenders like Intuitive; outsourcing 15-20% productivity; R&D/SG&A frugal teams bioresorbables. Fueled 300 bps op margin to 22.5% Q2, FY 23-24% ahead consensus.

Finally, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

We're reaffirming FY2024 guidance: revenue $5.25-$5.40 billion, 8-11% reported/7-10% organic; adj gross 68-69% +50-100 bps; op margin 24-25%; adj EPS $4.55-$4.75. Incorporates $1.2 billion NeuroPulse acquisition adding neuromodulation, no further M&A.

Built on Cardiovascular 45%, Endoscopy 25%, Ortho/Spine 20%, tailwinds structural heart, robotics, value-based. Organic 7-10%: mid-single procedures, 5-7% U.S. minimally invasive per Medtronic/BSCI trends; ASP flat to +1% reimbursement offset premium next-gen.

Cardio 9-12%: EvoHeart TAVR 18% U.S. share up from 14%, EVO-3 15% lower leak vs. Edwards Sapien; 12% U.S. TAVR STS data; WATCHMAN FLX Pro 25% LAAC EU AFib. Endoscopy 6-8%: GastroScope 360 AI 95% polyp sensitivity vs. GI Genius; 4% colonoscopy rebound, 10% U.S. ASP single-use pass-through. Ortho/Spine 5-7% +2 NeuroPulse: 8% robotic spine SynthoRobotics da Vinci compat; 12% lumbar NanoFuse CMS.

New ramps 2-3 points: PulseWave hypertension PMA Q4, FlexiCath APAC; $150 million value-based up 25% like Stryker bundles.

Gross 68-69%: 200 bps mix high-margin disposables 65% up 62%, $50 million Shenzhen savings -15% resin; 50 bps variances offset 10% Mexico tariffs.

OpEx: R&D 13.5% $710-730 million flat % for 15 Phase III incl. AI hemodynamic wearable; SG&A 18.5-19% digital sales 5% productivity 2,000 field; interest $120 million $3.5 billion debt 4.2%.

Regions: U.S. 65% 9-12% stable CMS TAVR $3,500, endoscopy pass-through, 3% Medicare Adv 50% volume. Europe 20% 5-7% MDR recert 80%, EvoHeart HTA Euro 1.08. APAC/EM 15% 12-15% China FlexiCath Q3 NMPA, India 500 hospitals, Japan WATCHMAN $80 million RMB 7.2.

Strategic: 300 bps share Precision Therapy AI cloud like Abbott Navitor; VitalCloud 20% EvoHeart connected -25% readmits; 50% plastics cut EU Green; Intuitive $100 million hybrid, Philips cath labs.

Risks: 1% FX -50 bps revenue; Taiwan chips -100 bps margin, dual 80%; PulseWave delay -$50 million; upside China tenders/IRA $100 million. Macro U.S. GDP +2.1%, medtech +5.5% Evaluate, electives 95% pre-COVID, inflation 2.5%.

Confident in $120 billion TAM 6% CAGR, 15% ROIC.

I will now turn the call over to Michael for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena outlined comprehensively, we delivered solid financial performance this quarter. Q2 revenue hit $1.31 billion, up 11% reported and 10% organic, driven by the procedure strength, new launches, and mix shifts she detailed. Gross profit was $892 million at 68.1%, aligning with our trends. Operating income adjusted $312 million, margin 23.8%. Diluted EPS adjusted $1.12, up 14%. Cash flow from operations $245 million, supporting $150 million share repurchases. Balance sheet strong with $1.2 billion cash, net debt to EBITDA 2.1x post-NeuroPulse.

For full-year, as reaffirmed, $5.25-5.40 billion revenue, etc., with assumptions fully transparent per Elena. Q3 outlook: revenue $1.35-1.38 billion, 9-12% growth; gross margin 68.3-68.8%; op margin 24.2%. These bake in continued procedure recovery, mix favorability, and efficiencies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for PulseWave neuromodulator, which is showing promising results in hypertension management with early data indicating 25% blood pressure reductions sustained at 12 months, positioning it for U.S. PMA Q4. Building on launches like VitaFlow Neo and CoreBot, our Phase III pipeline includes 15 trials: AI hemodynamic wearable for remote monitoring, reducing readmits 25%; bioresorbable peripheral stents IDE filed; Gen3 neuromod leads with 30% better battery life. R&D spend $180 million Q2, 13.7% revenue, funding Precision Therapy ecosystem integrating AI analytics for predictive outcomes. NeuroPulse integration accelerates neuromodulation, with SynthoRobotics compatibility expanding robotics to spine and ortho. Sustainability: 50% plastics reduction via bioresorbables qualifying EU Green subsidies. Partnerships with Intuitive and Philips enhance hybrid robotics and imaging. Pipeline de-risked, targeting 25% new product mix 2025, expanding adjacencies.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. Elena, on procedure volumes, with U.S. at 18.5% growth but Europe lagging, how do you see the recovery playing out in H2, especially with NHS issues?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, David. U.S. momentum continues with OPPS stability and IDN bundles, guiding 17-19% H2. Europe asynchronous: Germany/France strong on HTA/TAVR, UK stabilizing post-strikes with NICE neuromod gains. Overall H2 global 14-16%, 75% recovery complete, insulated by 65% recurring.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Gupta with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Priya Gupta:
Michael, on consumables mix hitting 68%, can you quantify the impact from NeuroPulse and forward outlook?

Michael Chen:
Absolutely, Priya. NeuroPulse instantly adds 300 bps via high-margin DBS leads, with $150 million annualized. Combined with Apex TAVR utilization 92% and FlexiMap share, FY24 68-69%, 14-16% growth. Utilization to 1.25x via MediConnect drives flywheel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
For new launches, VitaFlow Neo's 12% Europe share—Lisa, what's commercial traction and ramp risks?

Lisa Ramirez:
Thanks, Alex. Surgeon adoption accelerating on TRIDENT-2 best-in-class data, EU tenders adding 25% sequential. U.S. Medicare ASP +3.2% unlocks IDNs. Risks mitigated by inventory buffers, partnerships like Mindray in APAC doubling ortho sales. Targeting 15% robotics ortho share 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jordan Kim:
Raj, on R&D, PulseWave PMA Q4—any clinical updates and how it fits guidance assumptions?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Jordan, PulseWave pilots show 25% BP reduction, on track Q4 PMA contributing 2 points growth as assumed. Fits Precision Therapy with VitalCloud connectivity, 15 Phase III including wearables. No heroic bets, steady 6% TAM CAGR execution.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
